bug_description.normalized: The saved `xst` witness reaches JSX child lexing and accumulates attacker-controlled child text in `parser->buffer` until `p` reaches `q = parser->buffer + parser->bufferSize - 1`, the slot reserved for the terminating NUL. When the next child character is `&`, `fxGetNextTokenJSXChild()` dispatches into `fxGetNextEntity()` with that full-buffer state. `fxGetNextEntity()` then writes `*p++ = '&'` without the `p < q` guard used elsewhere, consuming the reserved terminator slot and advancing `p` to `q + 1`. The saved PoC contains no `&#` byte pairs, so the byte following the crashing `&` is proven only to be non-`#` and control enters the `else` branch; its guarded copy loop copies nothing because `p < q` is already false. The helper still executes `*p = 0`, so the NUL terminator is written one byte past the heap buffer and ASAN reports a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow at `xs/sources/xsLexical.c:1689`. The fix adds `if (p < q)` before the initial `&` write and skips the later `bsearch()` when no entity bytes fit.

source.description: First project statement that copies attacker-controlled JSX child bytes into the parser buffer whose occupancy later reaches the full-buffer `p == q` state used by the vulnerable entity path.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` is a 100021-byte `xst` script with JSX content. Repeated executions of this statement materialize one child-text token into `parser->buffer` until `p == q`; the next child character is `&`, which routes that full buffer into `fxGetNextEntity()`.

sink.description: ASAN crash site. After the unguarded `&` write advances `p` to `q + 1`, this unconditional terminator store performs the observed 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow.
sink.note: Both `reproduction_report.json` and `sanitizer_trace.txt` identify `fxGetNextEntity -> fxGetNextTokenJSXChild -> fxJSXElement` and report the write at `xsLexical.c:1689`.

root_cause.description: Missing bounds check. `fxGetNextEntity()` assumes there is still payload room and writes `&` even when `p == q`, consuming the reserved terminator slot and advancing `p` past the end before the later `*p = 0` write. The fix wraps this store in `if (p < q)` and also skips `bsearch()` when nothing fit.
root_cause.note: This direct store bypasses the `fxUTF8Buffer()` size check used by `fxGetNextTokenJSXChild()` for ordinary JSX child bytes, so it can move `p` beyond the last valid terminator slot.

tainted_value_origin.description: JSX child bytes from the attacker-controlled script are copied into `parser->buffer` here; repeated calls create the vulnerability-relevant occupancy state `p == q` before the later `&` entity.

parser_admitted.description: The witness successfully parses into a JSX element and enters child-token lexing, the only path in this trace that calls the vulnerable `fxGetNextEntity()` helper from JSX child text.

coarse_trace.summary: The `xst` fuzz target configures a 64 KiB parser buffer and `fxInitializeParser()` allocates the heap buffer that ASAN later reports as overflowing.

The witness reaches JSX child lexing, which uses `p = parser->buffer`, `q = p + parser->bufferSize - 1`, and appends child bytes until the token has filled the buffer up to the reserved terminator slot.
An `&` seen when `p == q` dispatches into entity parsing; the unguarded `*p++ = '&'` consumes the reserved NUL slot and advances `p` to `q + 1`.

The non-`#` entity branch then skips its guarded copy loop because `p < q` is already false, but it still executes `*p = 0`, writing one byte past the heap buffer exactly where ASAN reports the overflow.

fine_trace.note: The vulnerable parser allocates the heap buffer used by JSX child lexing. In the staged `xst` target `bufferSize` is 64 * 1024, and ASAN reports the overflow at the end of the resulting `sizeof(txParserChunk) + 65536 == 65544` byte allocation from `fxNewParserChunk()`.

fine_trace.code:
txString p = parser->buffer;
txString q = p + parser->bufferSize - 1;
fine_trace.note: The JSX child lexer starts writing at `parser->buffer` and derives `q` as the last byte reserved for the terminator; payload writes may advance `p` up to `q`, but the later `*p = 0` expects `p` itself to stay at or before `q`.

fine_trace.code:
p = fxUTF8Buffer(parser, parser->character, p, q);
fxGetNextCharacter(parser);
fine_trace.note: Source. Repeated executions of this ordinary-child path copy attacker-controlled JSX child bytes into `parser->buffer` through `fxUTF8Buffer()`, whose limit check keeps writes in-bounds while advancing `p` up to `q`. On the crashing witness this accumulation leaves `p == q` immediately before the next child character `&`.
When the next attacker-controlled child character is `&`, the switch dispatches into the entity parser with the already full-buffer state `p == q`.

Root cause. With `p == q`, this direct store writes `&` into the reserved terminator slot at `q` and advances `p` to `q + 1`; unlike `fxUTF8Buffer()`, it has no room check. The next line then loads the first entity byte for branch selection, and the fix adds `if (p < q)` before this store.

The saved `poc` contains no `&#` byte pairs, so after step 4 fetches the byte following the crashing `&`, this predicate is false for the crashing occurrence. Control therefore takes the `else` branch that ends with `*p = 0`.

In that non-`#` branch, the guarded copy loop is skipped immediately because step 4 already made `p < q` false before the first test. No additional entity byte is copied into the buffer, so `p` remains `q + 1` when execution reaches the terminator write.

Sink. The helper unconditionally writes the terminator at `q + 1`, and ASAN reports that exact 1-byte write at `0x631000010808`, the first byte past the 65544-byte parser-chunk allocation `[0x631000000800, 0x631000010808)`.

depends_on.via: while test fails immediately because !(p < q)

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. `reproduction_report.json` and `sanitizer_trace.txt` both pinpoint `xs/sources/xsLexical.c:1689` in `fxGetNextEntity`, which is the `*p = 0` sink recorded in fine-trace step 7.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. ASAN says the overflow is immediately past the parser buffer allocated by `fxNewParserChunk()`, and the missing `if (p < q)` before `*p++ = '&'` is exactly what moves `p` beyond that allocation's reserved terminator slot before the crashing write.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack `fxGetNextEntity -> fxGetNextTokenJSXChild -> fxJSXElement` matches the sink step, the caller that dispatches on `&`, and the JSX-element checkpoint in the trace.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The attacker-controlled JSX child bytes fill `parser->buffer` to `q`, the next attacker-controlled `&` enters `fxGetNextEntity()`, and the resulting `p == q + 1` state reaches the overflowing `*p = 0` write.

poc.trigger: The saved `poc` script is parsed by the staged vulnerable `xst` target; during JSX child lexing it reaches `fxGetNextEntity()` with `p == q` and crashes on the later `*p = 0` write.

format.name: Moddable JavaScript / JSX source
format.contract: The saved witness is a large `xst` source file that successfully reaches `fxJSXElement()` child lexing and accumulates one JSX child token until `p == parser->buffer + parser->bufferSize - 1` before the next child character `&` enters the non-`#` `fxGetNextEntity()` branch. The staged PoC contains no `&#` byte pairs, but it also contains many `&&` occurrences, so Stage 02 proves only that branch obligation and the resulting full-buffer-plus-`&` state; the exact post-`&` byte, numeric entities, and other neighboring JSX layouts were not independently validated.
